name: com.agenttoolyard/mcp
title: AgentToolyard
description: Twelve tools: exact money sums, ID checks, reconciliation, margin quotes and live URL checks.

tools.name: required_fields
tools.description: Use this to check whether a single record has the named keys, and that those values are not null. 0, false, and blank strings count as present. It does not check types or amounts, and it does not walk nested paths such as addr.zip.

tools.name: unique_ids
tools.description: Use this to find duplicate or missing identifiers in one list of rows. Comparison is exact and case-sensitive. IDs can be nonblank strings or integers. An integer beyond 2^53 is kept as its exact digits. The number 101 and the string "101" count as the same ID. If ID types are mixed, the warning lists row indexes whose type differs from the first valid ID. Do not use this to compare two lists; use reconcile_records when both sides share a unique ID.

items.description: The selected ID field accepts a nonblank string or an integer (digits kept exactly).

tools.name: exact_sum
tools.description: Use this to check whether a list of money amounts adds up to an expected total, using integer cents so 0.10 + 0.20 equals 0.30. Pass amounts and expected as decimal strings with at most two places, for example "0.10". One currency only; there is no currency field. Do not use this to compare two lists of records line by line; use reconcile_records for that. Do not use this to convert currencies.

items.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

expected.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

tools.name: row_count
tools.description: Use this only to check that a list you already have is the length you claimed. It does not prove a file or source system is complete.

tools.name: project_margin
tools.description: Use this when you already have both revenue and cost and want gross profit and gross margin in basis points. 2800 means 28.00%. Revenue and cost are decimal strings. Revenue must be positive. Do not use this to set a selling price from cost; use margin_price for that. For several cost what-ifs on fixed revenue, use scenario_margin.

revenue.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

cost.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

tools.name: reconcile_records
tools.description: Use this to match two lists of records by a shared unique ID and compare their money amounts exactly. Equal totals are not a pass if any line differs or is only on one side. Both lists must have unique IDs in id_field. Within each list, mixed-type warnings identify rows whose ID type differs from the first ID. Pass amounts as decimal strings. IDs can be nonblank strings or integers. An integer beyond 2^53 is kept as its exact digits. The number 101 and the string "101" count as the same ID. There is no currency field. Do not use this when the lists do not share an ID, when one payment covers several invoices, or when you need to match by date or name; no tool in this server does that. Do not use exact_sum just because the two totals are equal.

items.description: The selected ID field accepts a string or an integer (digits kept exactly). For the selected amount field, Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

The selected ID field accepts a string or an integer (digits kept exactly). For the selected amount field, Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

tools.name: acceptance_gate
tools.description: Use this to run several verification checks and pass only if every one of them passes. Each item in checks must be {"tool": name, "arguments": {...}}. Allowed tools are exact_sum, required_fields, unique_ids, row_count, and reconcile_records. A check can also include a label of up to 100 characters. Do not put pricing or margin tools here. Do not call this with an empty list. If one check is malformed, prefer this tool anyway rather than calling the checks separately, unless you cannot form the checks array.

tools.name: margin_price
tools.description: Use this when you know cost and want the lowest price that yields a target gross margin. target_margin_bps is basis points, not percent: 30% is 3000, not 30. 10% is 1000. Cost is a decimal string and must be positive. Do not use this if you already have a selling price and want the resulting margin; use project_margin. If you also have hours, a rate, expenses, and a contingency, use change_order instead.

cost.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

tools.name: change_order
tools.description: Use this to price added labor and expenses with a contingency and a target margin. hours must be a whole number. hourly_cost and expenses are decimal strings. contingency_bps and target_margin_bps are basis points, not percent: 10% is 1000, 30% is 3000. This is a model, not a reading of a contract. If you only have a lump-sum cost and a target margin, and no hours or contingency, use margin_price.

hourly_cost.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

expenses.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

tools.name: scenario_margin
tools.description: Use this when revenue is fixed and you want profit and margin at several explicit cost changes in one call. Pass cost_deltas as signed decimal strings, for example "-5000.00", "0.00", "10000.00". It does not assign probabilities. For a single revenue and cost with no what-ifs, use project_margin.

revenue.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

base_cost.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

items.description: Use decimal strings for exact values. Numbers must have magnitude below 1000000000000000, and String(n) must use plain decimal notation with at most 15 integer digits and 2 fractional digits. JSON numeric tokens must retain their decimal value when converted to Number.

tools.name: verify_live
tools.description: Check that a live URL returns what a deploy was supposed to produce. HTTPS URLs only. Up to 10 checks per call and 5 per host. Limit: 20 fetches per minute. Each check can expect a status, redirect location, headers, page title and text. Verdicts: pass means every expectation held. fail means the page answered and something did not match, or the URL is not allowed; the failures list says what, including the title actually found. inconclusive means the page could not be judged, for example a bot challenge or security checkpoint, a timeout, or a body cut off at 512 KB. Treat inconclusive as unknown, not as pass or fail.

tools.name: check_freshness
tools.description: Tell whether a cited source page still says what you quoted. HTTPS URLs only. Up to 10 sources per call and 5 per host. Limit: 20 fetches per minute. Each source can expect quoted snippets or a SHA-256 of the page. Verdicts: unchanged means the quoted snippets are still on the page (or the hash matches). changed means the page answered but a snippet is missing or the hash differs. fail means the URL is not allowed, for example it is not HTTPS or points at a private address. inconclusive means the page could not be judged, for example a bot challenge, an error status, a timeout or a truncated body. Treat inconclusive as unknown.
